title: pandas: new and changed columns
source:
import pandas as pd

plots = pd.read_csv("farm.csv").head(6)
plots["yield_per_mm"] = plots["yield_kg"] / plots["rainfall_mm"]
plots["yield_kg"] = plots["yield_kg"] * 2
plots.loc[1, "crop"] = "millet"
tons = plots.assign(yield_t=plots["yield_kg"] / 1000)

steps.narration: Read the CSV file "farm.csv" and kept its first 6 rows: plots is a new DataFrame, 6 rows × 6 columns, labelled 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Added the column yield_per_mm to plots: one value per row, from plots["yield_kg"] / plots["rainfall_mm"] (dtype float64).
Replaced the column yield_kg of plots with plots["yield_kg"] * 2: 5 of the 6 rows changed value.
Set one value of plots with loc: row 1, column crop, beans → millet.
tons is a new DataFrame, 6 rows × 8 columns: plots with the new column yield_t added.
